title: Major Deities of Ancient Egypt
notes: Egyptian mythology varied by location and historical period. Relationships, roles, and symbols could differ between traditions.

deities.name: Ra
deities.description: A major sun god associated with creation and kingship.
deities.notes: Also spelled Re. Often merged with other deities, including Amun and Horus.

relationships.relationship: Sometimes described as his daughter or the Eye of Ra

deities.duty: Travel across the sky by day and through the underworld by night.
deities.strength: A supreme divine power in many traditions, especially through his association with the sun.

deities.name: Amun
deities.description: A creator and king of the gods, particularly important at Thebes.
deities.notes: His name is often interpreted as 'the hidden one.' He was commonly combined with Ra as Amun-Ra.
deities.duty: Support the king and maintain divine order.
deities.strength: One of Egypt's most influential gods, especially during the New Kingdom.

deities.name: Osiris
deities.description: God of the dead, resurrection, and the afterlife.
deities.notes: His death and restoration are central themes in Egyptian mythology.
deities.duty: Rule the realm of the dead and preside over the afterlife.
deities.strength: A central authority over death, rebirth, and the fate of the deceased.

deities.name: Isis
deities.description: A goddess of magic, healing, motherhood, and royal protection.
deities.notes: Her worship spread beyond Egypt into the wider Mediterranean world.
deities.duty: Protect her family, assist the dead, and safeguard kingship.
deities.strength: Especially powerful in magic and protective spells.

deities.name: Horus
deities.description: A falcon god associated with the sky and divine kingship.
deities.notes: Several forms of Horus existed. Horus the Younger is commonly described as the son of Isis and Osiris.

relationships.relationship: Mother, in the Horus the Younger tradition
Father, in the Horus the Younger tradition
Uncle and adversary in the struggle for kingship

deities.duty: Protect the king and uphold legitimate rule.
deities.strength: A powerful defender of kingship and order.

deities.name: Set
deities.description: A god associated with deserts, storms, strength, and disorder.
deities.notes: Set could be both a dangerous adversary and a protector. In some traditions, he defended Ra's solar boat.
deities.duty: Defend the solar boat in some traditions and embody dangerous forces beyond ordered life.
deities.strength: Known for exceptional physical power and combat ability.

deities.name: Anubis
deities.description: A funerary god associated with embalming and the protection of graves.
deities.notes: Often represented as a black jackal or as a jackal-headed man.
deities.duty: Oversee mummification and assist in the judgment of the deceased.
deities.strength: A leading protector of tombs and funerary rites.

deities.name: Thoth
deities.description: A god of writing, wisdom, calculation, and the moon.
deities.notes: Traditionally credited with knowledge of writing and sacred texts.

relationships.relationship: Associated with truth and cosmic order; sometimes described as his consort
Served as a divine adviser and scribe in some traditions

deities.duty: Record divine decisions and the results of the judgment of the dead.
deities.strength: Highly powerful through knowledge, speech, and magical expertise.

deities.name: Hathor
deities.description: A goddess of love, music, joy, motherhood, and the sky.
deities.notes: She had both nurturing and fierce aspects and was sometimes identified with the Eye of Ra.

relationships.relationship: Sometimes described as his daughter or the Eye of Ra
Associated as consort in some local traditions

deities.duty: Nurture gods and people, welcome the dead, and support celebration and kingship.
deities.strength: A broad and influential goddess with both protective and destructive manifestations.

deities.name: Bastet
deities.description: A goddess associated with protection, the household, and cats.
deities.notes: Earlier forms could be lioness-headed; later depictions commonly show her as a cat or cat-headed woman.

relationships.relationship: Another fierce solar goddess with overlapping roles

deities.duty: Protect households and temples and defend against harmful forces.
deities.strength: A protective goddess capable of fierce defense.

deities.name: Sekhmet
deities.description: A lioness goddess associated with warfare, destructive heat, and healing.
deities.notes: Her name means 'the powerful one.' She could bring disease as well as protect against it.

relationships.relationship: Often described as his daughter and an Eye of Ra

deities.duty: Defend Ra and the king, punish enemies, and protect against illness.
deities.strength: Among the fiercest and most destructive Egyptian deities.

deities.name: Maat
deities.description: The goddess and personification of truth, justice, and cosmic order.
deities.notes: Maat also refers to the principle of proper order in the universe and society.

relationships.relationship: Associated with him through truth and order

deities.duty: Maintain order and provide the standard used in judging the dead.
deities.strength: Represents a foundational principle on which Egyptian cosmic and social order depended.

deities.name: Ptah
deities.description: A creator god and patron of craftspeople, especially important at Memphis.
deities.notes: In Memphite theology, he creates through thought and speech.
deities.duty: Create and sustain the world and protect artisans.
deities.strength: A major creator deity whose divine thought and speech bring things into being.

deities.name: Nut
deities.description: The sky goddess, often depicted arching over the earth.
deities.notes: She was believed to swallow the sun at evening and give birth to it again at dawn.
deities.duty: Form the heavens and participate in the daily rebirth of the sun.
deities.strength: A cosmic deity whose body represents the sky itself.

deities.name: Geb
deities.description: The god of the earth.
deities.notes: He was sometimes depicted lying beneath Nut, separated from her by Shu.
deities.duty: Embody and sustain the earth.
deities.strength: A foundational cosmic deity associated with the land and royal inheritance.

deities.name: Nephthys
deities.description: A protective goddess associated with mourning, funerary rites, and the dead.
deities.notes: Often shown with Isis as a protector and mourner of Osiris.
deities.duty: Protect the deceased and assist in funerary rituals.
deities.strength: Especially important as a protective and funerary deity.

deities.name: Khnum
deities.description: A ram-headed creator god associated with the Nile and the formation of living beings.
deities.notes: In some traditions, he shaped bodies on a potter's wheel.

relationships.relationship: Associated as a daughter in the Elephantine triad

deities.duty: Form living beings and watch over the Nile's waters.
deities.strength: A powerful creator and guardian of a life-giving water source.

deities.name: Sobek
deities.description: A crocodile god associated with water, fertility, strength, and royal protection.
deities.notes: His character combined the danger of crocodiles with their perceived strength and protective power.

relationships.relationship: Combined with him as Sobek-Ra in some traditions

deities.duty: Protect the king and sacred places and support fertility.
deities.strength: A formidable protective deity associated with the power of the crocodile.

deities.name: Neith
deities.description: An ancient goddess associated with warfare, weaving, and creation.
deities.notes: Her importance and roles varied across Egyptian history, with a major cult center at Sais.

relationships.relationship: Associated with creation and the early gods in some traditions

deities.duty: Protect the dead and the divine order; serve as a creator in some traditions.
deities.strength: An ancient and powerful goddess with both creative and martial roles.

deities.name: Shu
deities.description: A god of air and the space between earth and sky.
deities.notes: He is often depicted holding Nut above Geb.
deities.duty: Hold up the sky and maintain the space needed for life.
deities.strength: A foundational cosmic deity whose support sustains the heavens.

deities.name: Tefnut
deities.description: A goddess commonly associated with moisture and a member of the Heliopolitan creation tradition.
deities.notes: Her exact characteristics and interpretations vary in surviving sources.
deities.duty: Participate in creation and help sustain the natural and divine order.
deities.strength: An early cosmic goddess with protective and sometimes fierce aspects.

deities.name: Khonsu
deities.description: A moon god associated with time, healing, and protection.
deities.notes: His name is often understood as 'the traveler,' referring to the moon's movement.
deities.duty: Travel across the sky as the moon and protect those in need.
deities.strength: A prominent lunar deity with significant healing and protective roles.

deities.name: Mut
deities.description: A mother goddess and queenly deity especially important at Thebes.
deities.notes: Her name means 'mother.' She could be represented as a woman or as a lioness-headed goddess.
deities.duty: Protect the king and act as a divine mother and consort.
deities.strength: A major royal and protective goddess, especially at Thebes.

deities.name: Atum
deities.description: A creator and sun god prominent in the theology of Heliopolis.
deities.notes: Often associated with the setting sun and with the completion of creation.

relationships.relationship: Combined with him in the form Ra-Atum

deities.duty: Bring the first gods into being and participate in the solar cycle.
deities.strength: A primeval creator deity and source of the Heliopolitan divine family.
